findings_and_connected_questions.title: Match-pattern fingerprinting removes spaces inside string literals
findings_and_connected_questions.trace: For a match arm, visit_expr_match converts the pattern to tokens, compact_tokens removes every ASCII space from the resulting token text, and quoted_strings reparses that text before reading string literals. Thus spaces inside literals are removed along with formatting whitespace. The current corpse source matches left arm and right arm, while the exact current baseline rows record leftarm and rightarm. The FBX match accepts Lcl Translation, while its collect_layer baseline records LclTranslation; the separate if-let takes path and baseline retain the spaced spelling. validate_findings keys baseline occurrences by rule, path, item and fingerprint.
findings_and_connected_questions.conditions: The source establishes a lossy identity transform and matching baseline examples. A whitespace-only alteration of a match literal can leave the same normalized fingerprint and count when the same scope still allows the finding and rule/path/item and other occurrences stay unchanged; that is conditional static reasoning, not an observed edit, executed scanner, stale-check result or validated product incident. Different values can collapse only within the same finding key fields; the example contrasts source and metadata without asserting an actual duplicate entry.
findings_and_connected_questions.future_repair_direction: Extract literal values directly from the original syntax tree rather than whitespace-normalized source text, preserve exact decoded string identity and intentionally retain native format boundaries. Reconcile impacted existing baseline keys and count changes as part of the later authorized repair; do not weaken deliberate boundary-adapter scopes or treat a baseline tuple alone as a product defect.
relationships: 059 q3442 reviewed complete e275 catalogue as metadata and explicitly left the named scanner/actual implementation independent; it did not prove this 95e consumer behavior. Segovb READ-L11-402 inspected the 6533 baseline and analyzer/config but did not credit scan.rs body or identify this exact match-pattern first failure. Targeted historical inventories located the relevant old tuples but no proven exact alias; central owns full reconciliation.
